messages:
leo: Hi everyone, first-week kube hiccup. My kubeconfig uses SSH certificate auth (`exec` -> `ssh-cert-helper`) and `kubectl get ns` returns `exec plugin: failed to exec: ssh: signer unknown`. I'm on macOS Ventura, installed helper via brew. Any quick fixes?

marie: Welcome, leo! That error usually means your ssh-agent doesn't have the signing key loaded. Start with `ssh-add -l` to list identities. If empty, `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_redwood_cert` (or the path from your onboarding key bundle).

leo: `ssh-add -l` says "The agent has no identities." I added the cert with `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_redwood_cert` then retried, but now `kubectl get ns` fails with `exec plugin: invalid certificate: certificate expired`. Looks like the cert is time-limited.

marie: Yep, we issue short-lived SSH certs (72h) for kube exec. You can request a new cert from the Access Portal (onboarding has a "Request SSH cert" button) or use the CLI helper `redwood-access request-cert --reason "kube onboarding"`. The portal returns the key/cert and updates your kubeconfig automatically if you choose that option.

access-bot: Note: SSH cert rotation requires MFA. Portal: https://onboard.redwood.ai/access -> Request > SSH cert. TTL max 72h.

leo: I tried `redwood-access request-cert` and it failed with `401 unauthorized` from the dev container. Is there a workaround?

nora: If you're in a devcontainer, that CLI needs the container to share your browser auth. Quick workaround is to run the CLI on your host and copy the `~/.ssh/id_redwood_cert` into the container. Or open the portal in your browser and download the cert bundle, then `ssh-add` the cert inside the container.

leo: Downloaded cert bundle from portal and `ssh-add`ed inside the container. `kubectl get ns` now shows namespaces. One more question: I still get `Forbidden` for `kubectl get pods -n infra-tools`. How do I request namespace access for cert-auth users?

marie: We tie SSH cert subjects to GitHub usernames and RBAC via the Access repo. For namespace access you can open an Access Portal request (select "Namespace role for user/cert") or create a tiny PR in infra/access-requests with a RoleBinding YAML. Include your GitHub handle and cert subject (should be auto-populated if you used the portal). Tag @marie for review.

leo: Created portal request and a PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4799 - requested `view` on `infra-tools`.

access-bot: Access request created: infra PR #4799 by leo. Reviewer: marie.

marie: Approved and applied. You should have `view` in `infra-tools` now. Check with `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n infra-tools`.

ops-bot: Permission change applied by marie at 1806001153.

leo: `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n infra-tools` -> "yes". All set, thanks! :tada:
